quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: If you shift into a lower gear while not going slow enough, what happens?

options.text: The motorcycle lurches and the rear tire skids.
The front tire will likely skid.
The engine makes a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle lurches and the rear tire skids.
questions.explanation: If you shift into a lower gear while riding too fast, the motorcycle will lurch and the rear tire may skid.

questions.question: When riding at night, what should you do?

options.text: Avoid using your high beam headlight.

questions.explanation: It is harder to judge distances in the dark than in daylight. Slow down and increase your following distance at night. Use your high beam anytime you are not meeting or following another vehicle.

questions.question: Which of these gives a rider the best protection?
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield or eyeglasses do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle, what is best?

options.text: Let one rider fully pass before the next rider begins to pass.
Let several riders pass the vehicle at the same time.
Have the last rider wave to show no other motorcycles are coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let one rider fully pass before the next rider begins to pass.
questions.explanation: Riders in a group should pass one at a time. Each rider should finish passing and get back in formation before the next rider passes.

questions.question: How do you stay in control while turning?

options.text: Speed up before entering the turn.
Look through the turn to plan your path.
Come to a complete stop before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the turn to plan your path.
questions.explanation: To stay in control through a turn, look through the turn by turning only your head. Slow down before the turn and lean your motorcycle in the right direction.

questions.question: If you are riding beside another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Stay alongside until the next exit.
Let the other driver worry about it.

questions.explanation: Riding beside another vehicle is dangerous because you may be in its blind spot. The vehicle could also block your escape route. Speed up or drop back to get away from the vehicle.

questions.question: If a tire is flat and you must brake, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
Apply the brake of the tire that is flat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, slowly apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.

questions.question: The front brake provides about how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. The front brake provides at least 70 percent of the total stopping power.

questions.question: Which of these should a face shield NOT be to be effective?

options.text: Allow clear views to both sides

questions.explanation: A face shield should be scratch-free, allow clear side views, fasten securely, and allow air to pass through. An airtight face shield causes fogging and makes it hard to see.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, what should you do?

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest.

questions.explanation: Dogs are often attracted to motorcycles. If chased by a dog, downshift and approach it slowly. Then speed up and leave it behind.

questions.question: A person is considered legally intoxicated with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______.
questions.explanation: In Kentucky, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to drive while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: A motorcycle with a sidecar:

options.text: Can tip over if making a turn too fast.
Is designed to take corners at any speed.
Should not be used for loading items.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can tip over if making a turn too fast.
questions.explanation: Even with three wheels on the ground, a motorcycle with a sidecar can tip over if you turn too sharply or go too fast around a corner.

questions.question: When riding near stopped or slow-moving cars, a motorcyclist should:

options.text: Pull over and wait until traffic begins to move.
Ride on the shoulder to get through the area as quickly as possible.
Weave between the cars to get through the area as quickly as possible.

questions.explanation: Weaving between slowed or parked cars is dangerous. You could hit an opening car door or a car pulling into traffic. You won't have room to escape if a hazard appears. Never ride on the shoulder because other drivers won't expect you there.

questions.question: Before carrying a passenger in traffic for the first time, you should:

options.text: Practice riding on an empty road.
Flash your lights so others can see you.
Practice riding on the shoulder of a road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice riding on an empty road.
questions.explanation: Before riding with a passenger or carrying heavy cargo in traffic, practice on a quiet road. This helps you learn how your motorcycle handles the extra weight.

questions.question: A proper lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Communicate your intentions to other road users.

questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen. It helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It also discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if needed. However, lane position does not help you avoid traffic signals.

questions.question: To increase your visibility, you should:

options.text: Turn off your headlight during the day.
Keep your headlight on at all times.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on at all times.
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright and reflective clothing, keep your headlight on all the time, and change your lane position as needed.

questions.question: A group of riders should merge onto a highway in:
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is normally best while riding. However, when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway, riders should switch to a single-file formation.

questions.question: The best way to stop quickly is to:

options.text: Throttle down and use the front brake.

questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both brakes at the same time. Apply the brakes firmly. Do not panic if the brakes lock.

questions.question: When braking, you should use:

options.text: Either the front or rear brake, but not both.

questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, you should:

options.text: Ride in a position that will allow the other driver to see you in their rearview mirror.
Ride in the far left portion of the lane.
Ride in the far right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a position that will allow the other driver to see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Position your motorcycle so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Riding in the center of the lane usually puts you in the middle of their mirror, where they are most likely to notice you.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT protective clothing for motorcyclists?
questions.explanation: A leather jacket, long denim pants, and full-fingered gloves protect motorcyclists during falls. Motorcyclists should wear lace-up boots, high-top boots, or heavy shoes that support the ankles. Athletic shoes do not provide this protection.

questions.question: A helmet should NOT:

options.text: Have been worn in a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have been worn in a crash.
questions.explanation: A good helmet meets U.S. DOT standards, fits snugly, and has no obvious defects. If a helmet has been worn during a crash, it should be replaced.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle on a two-lane road, they should:

options.text: Pass in a staggered formation with several riders at once.

questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, riders should pass one at a time. Each rider must finish their pass before the next rider begins.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume the motorcycle is as easy to see as other vehicles.
Assume other drivers cannot see you.
Not worry about whether other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume other drivers cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and have few lights compared to other vehicles, making them hard to see. Ride defensively and assume other drivers do not see you.
